messages.subject: Unknown IO Error
parts:
G'day Nichemappers,

In the long run I guess Mike is going to field this and many other questions that make it to this forum, but maybe somebody else has had this problem as well.

Ultimately my aim is to import my own climate data into NicheMapR and run a few high resolution, small-scale models. Before I can do that I thought I'd run the tutorials so that I understand the data structures that I'll be playing with. I've read the various vignettes and docs, I've downloaded the climate data from the CAMEL website, I've installed it where it should be installed (I think), and yet I keep hitting a glitch at the second step of the microclimate modelling tutorial. Transcript is below:

> library(NicheMapR)
> micro<-micro_global(loc="Madison, Wisconsin, USA")
No such file or directoryUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorUnknown IO errorfailed to load external entity "http://maps.google.com/maps/api/geocode/xml?address=Madison,Wisconsin,USA&sensor=false"
Error : 1: No such file or directory2: Unknown IO error3: Unknown IO error4: Unknown IO error5: Unknown IO error6: Unknown IO error7: Unknown IO error8: Unknown IO error9: Unknown IO error10: Unknown IO error11: Unknown IO error12: Unknown IO error13: Unknown IO error14: Unknown IO error15: Unknown IO error16: failed to load external entity "http://maps.google.com/maps/api/geocode/xml?address=Madison,Wisconsin,USA&sensor=false"

Error: object 'doc' not found

>

Has anybody else seen this? It looks like the micro_global call is reaching for a google maps link, but because I can't get inside the call and see what it's doing, I have no idea exactly what kind of data it's looking for. If the NicheMapR climate always opens up a google search, how does one import unique climate layers into it? I can see from the other forum posts that some of you have pulled this off, so I figure somebody has figured out a workaround for this glitch. Any help will be great. Cheers

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Unknown IO Error
parts:
Hi Sean,

Were you connected to the internet at the time? Looks like you might not have been, and so the Google Earth search option would have failed.

Try it again specifying a longitude and latitude for the variable 'loc', e.g.

micro<-micro_global(loc=c(145,-35))

See the help for micro_global:
loc

 Either a longitude and latitude (decimal degrees) or a place name to search for on Google Earth


Also, you can see the code of micro_global (or any other R function) by just typing its name or using the edit function.

All the best,
Mike
